waypoints.name: White River Campground (Glacier Basin Trailhead)
waypoints.directions: From Enumclaw drive SR 410 east about 43 miles to the White River Entrance. Turn right on the Sunrise road, take the signed White River Campground turnoff, cross the White River and follow the campground road to its end at about 4,300 ft. Park in the day-hiking and climbing lot; the trail starts in Loop D. The road is open only in summer, typically June to October, and a park entrance pass is required.

waypoints.name: Glacier Basin Camp Site Area
waypoints.directions: Take the Glacier Basin Trail up the north side of the Inter Fork of the White River on an old mining road grade. At about 0.9 mile stay right where the Emmons Moraine Trail branches left across the river, and continue past creek crossings and slide paths to Glacier Basin Campground at the end of the maintained trail, about 3.5 miles.

waypoints.name: Camp Schurman
waypoints.directions: Follow the climbers' path about a mile up the lateral moraine to the toe of the Inter Glacier near 7,000 ft, rope up and climb between the two nunataks, trending left to Camp Curtis on the rocky ridge near 8,700 ft. From there traverse down and right onto the Emmons Glacier and around the south side of Steamboat Prow, about half a mile, to the ranger hut at Camp Schurman.

waypoints.name: Emmons Glacier Corridor
waypoints.directions: Leave Camp Schurman straight up the Emmons Glacier to Emmons Flats, a level bench just above Steamboat Prow. Continue up toward the crater rim, weaving around crevasses, until a snow ramp lets you move left near 10,200 ft onto the Corridor, a smooth rib of snow running up the fall line to roughly 11,600 ft.

waypoints.name: Columbia Crest
waypoints.directions: Where crevasses and seracs block the direct line at the top of the Corridor, angle climber's right into the broad apron below the saddle between Liberty Cap and the crater, switchbacking around crevasses to a ramp across the final bergschrund near 13,000 ft. Gain the crater rim and traverse to Columbia Crest. The line changes through the season, so keep a GPS track for the descent.

waypoints.name: Paradise Parking Area
waypoints.directions: From SR 706 at Ashford, drive east through the park's Nisqually Entrance and follow the Paradise Road past Longmire about 18 miles to Paradise. Climbers park in the upper Paradise lot by the visitor center at about 5,400 ft. A park entrance pass is required, plus the climbing registration and a wilderness permit for the high camps.

waypoints.name: Glacier Vista
waypoints.directions: Leave the upper Paradise lot on the Skyline Trail and follow the standard Muir-bound tread as it climbs above the meadows. Glacier Vista is the marked overlook where the Nisqually opens up several hundred feet below you. This is where the Kautz route leaves the trail system for good.

waypoints.name: Nisqually Glacier crossing
waypoints.directions: From Glacier Vista follow the climbers' path down the moraine to about 6,300 ft, where boot paths drop onto the Nisqually Glacier. Rope up here: the crossing threads crevassed ground under icefall and is dangerous in poor visibility.

waypoints.name: Wilson Gully
waypoints.directions: Take the line of least resistance across the glacier to its far side and the distinct low-angle snow gully there, then climb it to the bench above at roughly 7,300 to 7,400 ft. Keep well left of The Fan, the gully further down the glacier, which carries avalanche and rockfall. Move through this stretch early and do not stop in it.

waypoints.name: Lower Castle
waypoints.directions: From the bench, snow slopes lead up past the Wilson Moraine camps (8,200 to 8,600 ft) to the ridge and Lower Castle, a few closely spaced rock rings at about 9,200 ft.

waypoints.name: Upper Castle
waypoints.directions: A short way on up the ridge. Large rock rings, and where most parties spend the first night; running water is usually close by from mid-June. The Comet Falls way in joins here.

waypoints.name: Camp Hazard
waypoints.directions: Above the Castle the Turtle snowfield leads to Camp Hazard: sun-cupped firm snow and glacier ice, so keep an ice tool in hand. Stay to the west side of the snowfield, because its centre and east flank are raked by rock and ice off the Kautz Ice Cliff.

waypoints.name: Rock Step
waypoints.directions: From the top bivy sites a climbers' trail leads up and left to a notch on the ridge with a fixed rope on rock anchors. Rappel, or down-climb on belay, the short rock step below it into the gully under the ice cliff. You climb it again on the way back.

waypoints.name: Kautz Ice Chute (base)
waypoints.directions: From the foot of the step, traverse west under the Kautz Ice Cliff to the foot of the chute. This is the deposition zone under the ice cliff and the reason for the alpine start: cross it moving and do not stop.

waypoints.name: Top of the ice chute
waypoints.directions: The chute is two steps of ice separated by easier snow: the lower step AI2, the upper step the AI3 crux. Each is anything from a short pitch to a few hundred feet depending on the year, bare and hard in a lean year.

waypoints.name: Columbia Crest
waypoints.directions: Regroup above the chute and rope for glacier travel: the upper Kautz holds some of the mountain's biggest crevasses. Trend up and right to Wapowety Cleaver near 13,000 ft, watching for moats along the rock, then onto the upper Nisqually and past a large bergschrund near the crater rim before the flat walk to the top.

wa_mount_rainier_kautz_glacier.fa: Hans Fuhrer, Heinie Fuhrer, Roger Toll, and Harry Myers, June 26-28, 1920 (August Kautz's 1857 party reached ~12,000 ft on this line)

waypoints.name: Paradise
waypoints.directions: From SR 7 at Elbe, take SR 706 east through Ashford to the Nisqually Entrance, then follow the park road past Longmire to Paradise at about 5,400 ft, roughly 19 miles from the entrance. Overnight parking is allowed only in designated areas, and from November the road above Longmire is gated every night. A park entrance pass is required, plus a climbing permit for glacier travel or above 10,000 ft.

waypoints.name: Camp Muir
waypoints.directions: Take the Skyline Trail past Panorama Point to Pebble Creek near 7,200 ft, the last running water, then climb north up the unmarked Muir Snowfield above McClure Rock to Camp Muir, about 4.5 miles in all. In poor visibility hold 355 degrees true from Pebble Creek toward Moon Rocks; crevassed glaciers lie on both sides and a corniced cliff band sits between McClure and Anvil rocks.

waypoints.name: Columbia Crest
waypoints.directions: Leave camp northwest onto the Cowlitz Cleaver, not east toward Cathedral Gap, and climb past the Beehive and through a notch to the base of Gibraltar Rock near 11,800 ft. Traverse the ledges west along its foot, with one exposed downclimb and gully to regain them, into the Gibraltar Chute and up to Camp Comfort near 12,600 ft. Rope up across the upper Ingraham to the crater rim and cross the crater to Columbia Crest.

waypoints.name: North Fork Sauk River Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Darrington, drive the Mountain Loop Highway south about 16 miles to Forest Road 49 (Sloan Creek Road), turn east and drive about 6.4 miles to the North Fork Sauk Trailhead parking lot at about 2,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and a free Glacier Peak Wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

waypoints.name: North Fork Sauk Trail / PCT junction
waypoints.note: Top of the North Fork Sauk switchbacks. Turn north on the PCT here for Red Pass and the White Chuck valley; White Pass is a short way south and off this route.
waypoints.directions: Follow North Fork Sauk Trail #649 up the valley through old-growth forest, past the Red Creek bridge to Mackinaw Shelter at about 5.5 miles, then climb a long series of switchbacks to meet the Pacific Crest Trail in meadows at about 5,950 ft, roughly 8.5 miles from the car.

waypoints.name: Glacier Peak Summit
waypoints.directions: Turn north on the PCT over Red Pass and follow it down the upper White Chuck valley 7-9 miles, past the old White Chuck River Trail junction, to a forest camp near 4,100 ft by Sitkum Creek. Take the unsigned climbers' path straight up the ridge south of the creek to Boulder Basin, then head southeast up snowfields onto the Sitkum Glacier, climb it to the 9,500 ft saddle east of Sitkum Spire, and follow the pumice ridge to the summit.

waypoints.name: Hoh River Ranger Station
waypoints.directions: From US 101 about 13 miles south of Forks, turn east on Upper Hoh Road and drive about 18 miles to the road end at the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center, about 578 ft. A park entrance pass is required, and overnight trips need an Olympic National Park wilderness permit booked in advance; the Hoh is a quota area.

waypoints.name: Glacier Meadows
waypoints.directions: Follow the Hoh River Trail east up the valley past the Olympus Guard Station and Lewis Meadow, cross the High Hoh Bridge over the gorge, and climb past Elk Lake to Glacier Meadows at about 4,300 ft, roughly 17.5 miles. About a quarter mile below the meadows the trail crosses a washout on a ladder of roughly 100 ft with a fixed rope.

waypoints.name: Snow Dome
waypoints.directions: Take the climbers' way trail about 0.8 mile up onto the crest of the lateral moraine, follow the narrow, loose crest about 0.2 mile, then drop onto the toe of the Blue Glacier and rope up. Cross the glacier and climb roped to Snow Dome at about 6,600-6,800 ft.

waypoints.name: Mount Olympus (West Peak)
waypoints.directions: Stay roped and continue over Crystal Pass, scouting the large crevasse there for a usable snow bridge, then traverse south of and below Five Fingers Ridge toward the West Peak, which is hidden from the north. Cross the moat or bergschrund and climb the 80-ft summit tower by loose Class 4 ramps or the 5.4 north face.

waypoints.name: Heliotrope Ridge Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542), continue about 1 mile east of the Glacier Public Service Center and turn right onto Glacier Creek Road (FS 39). Drive about 8 miles, turn left at a junction and continue less than half a mile to the Heliotrope Ridge Trailhead for Trail 677, at about 3,700 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

waypoints.name: Hogsback Camp
waypoints.directions: Follow Trail 677 through old growth, crossing Grouse, Kulshan and Heliotrope Creeks (lowest early in the day), to the signed fork at about 2.25 miles. Go right on the climbers' path up the crest of the Hogsback moraine to the camps around 6,000 ft at the edge of the Coleman Glacier.

waypoints.name: North Ridge Base / Coleman Glacier Junction
waypoints.directions: Rope up and cross the Coleman Glacier east (climber's left) toward the toe of the North Ridge, threading seracs and open crevasses; the route changes yearly and often has no track. Arrive at the double bergschrund guarding the base of the ridge, and probe as you near it for a hidden third crack between the two visible ones.

waypoints.name: Mount Baker Summit
waypoints.directions: Cross the double bergschrund on a bridge or narrow ramp and climb the broad 40 degree snow gully to the ridge crest. Follow the crest to the ice cliff near 9,600 ft and climb its steep ice, short near-vertical steps then sustained 60 to 65 degree ice, for several pitches. Above it the angle eases; trend climber's left through crevasses on the upper ice cap to the summit plateau and Grant Peak.

waypoints.name: Shannon Ridge Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Drive Baker Lake Road (Forest Road 11) north from SR 20 near milepost 82, then turn onto FR 1152 and follow the 1152-014 spur to its end at about 2,500 feet, where the trail begins. The spur is rough and rutted, so high clearance is the sensible minimum for the drive in. If you're staying overnight in the park, you'll need a North Cascades backcountry permit, obtained in person at Marblemount or arranged with the wilderness office ahead of time.

waypoints.name: Timberline Junction
waypoints.directions: Follow Shannon Ridge Trail #742, an old roadbed heading northeast, for about 2 miles to where the road tread ends near 3,800 ft, weaving through a belt of blowdown. Continue on true trail angling left through brush onto the open ridge crest and up to timberline near 4,600 ft, where snow often lingers into midsummer.

waypoints.name: Shannon Ridge / Sulphide Glacier Camp
waypoints.directions: From timberline, follow the broad, rolling crest of Shannon Ridge through meadows and broken timber for about 2 miles to a pass near 5,400 ft, where a north-south ridge is met and the Sulphide Glacier and summit pyramid first come into view. Continue up open slopes and snow onto the toe of the glacier to the lower camp at about 6,200 ft; an upper camp sits near 6,500 ft. There is no reliable water late in the season.

waypoints.name: Mount Shuksan Summit Pyramid
waypoints.directions: Rope up at camp and climb north up the west side of the Sulphide Glacier over a series of rolling steps; near 7,600 ft the angle eases, so bear north-northeast across the upper glacier to the foot of the summit pyramid at about 8,400-8,500 ft. Cross the moat and climb the central gully on the pyramid's south face, the one with rappel anchors, roughly 600 ft of steep snow or blocky rock to the summit.

waypoints.name: Bedal Creek / Bedal Basin Trailhead (end of FR 4096)
waypoints.directions: Drive the Mountain Loop Highway to Forest Road 4096 and follow that rough, narrow spur - a 4WD road about three miles long where high clearance genuinely helps - to its end at the Bedal Creek trailhead, around 2,790 feet.

waypoints.name: Climber's trail turnoff on Bedal Creek Trail
waypoints.directions: Walk the old Bedal Creek Trail about 1.5 miles and 700 ft to around 3,500 ft, where a climbers' path, often marked with pink flagging, turns off to the left. Watch for it: the old tread continues and dies in a brushy washout below the basin.

waypoints.name: Sloan Peak Summit
waypoints.directions: Climb the path steeply through forest to talus near 4,900 ft, then bend southeast to the Bedal-Sloan saddle at 5,300 ft. Continue southeast over a rock ridge near 5,800 ft, rope up and cross the Sloan Glacier southwest to the rock near 7,100 ft. Follow the exposed heather shelf of the Corkscrew across the south face onto the west face, climb the gully to the crest, then a short class 4 step and third class to the summit.

road.name: Bedal Creek Trailhead (FR-4096), off Mountain Loop Highway
road.status: Mountain Loop Highway is paved from Granite Falls to Barlow Pass then unpaved for a stretch near Darrington; FR-4096 is a gravel spur ~18.25 mi south of Darrington, generally passable to standard cars in season but subject to washouts/seasonal closure.
road.driveNote: Roughly 1.5-2 hours from Seattle via US-2/SR-92/Mountain Loop Highway to the Bedal Creek Trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: FR roads off the Mountain Loop Highway are typically only reliably open late spring through fall; check Darrington Ranger District/USFS alerts for current status.

waypoints.name: Sunrise Mine Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east about 27 to 28 miles, then turn onto Sunrise Mine Road, Forest Road 4065. Follow roughly 2.3 to 2.5 miles of gravel to the road's end at the Sunrise Mine Trailhead, where Trail No. 707 starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

waypoints.name: Vesper Peak
waypoints.directions: Take Trail 707 across the unbridged South Fork Stillaguamish and up through forest and a talus basin to the steep, loose couloir and Headlee Pass, about 2.7 miles in. Traverse below Sperry Peak into the upper Vesper Creek basin, leave the lake trail at the creek crossing, and climb the steep bootpath to treeline, then about 1,000 ft of granite slabs on the central rib, following cairns, to the summit.

road.name: SR-20 / North Cascades Highway
road.status: Paved and open in summer; unmarked climbers' pullout near milepost 165-166.
road.driveNote: Park at the pullout near MP 165-166, about 4 miles east of Washington Pass, near the Silver Star trail sign.
road.seasonalGate: Gated for winter roughly early December through mid-April/May (closure points at MP 171 Silver Star gate and points further west/east depending on snowpack); confirm current status with WSDOT before an early- or late-season attempt.
